content.text: I have what I need. Let me record my assessment.

input.quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale:
Neither side has a convenience exit, so the rule's two halves land in opposite directions and I am escalating rather than redlining.

Vendor side — better than preferred. § 7.1 (p0314) bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer at all except where it is legally unable to perform, and even then § 7.3 (p0329) requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts, § 7.5 makes it cooperate on transition and bear transition expenses (p0347), and § 7.4(a)(ii) makes the Indenture Trustee automatic backstop servicer (p0335). The preferred position only asks that Vendor have "no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term"; this exceeds it.

Customer side — no convenience right. Removal is available only on a Servicer Termination Event, and then it is the Indenture Trustee acting at the direction of the Controlling Class, not the Issuer, who removes (§ 7.2(c), p0327). The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid off (§ 8.3, p0363), well beyond 12 months. Read literally against the detection guidance, that is the walk-away trigger ("No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term").

Why I am not redlining. (1) The harm the rule protects against is absent: the Servicing Fee accrues per Collection Period in return for performing its obligations (p0134), there are no prepaid fees, no minimum-term commitment and no early-termination fee anywhere, so there is nothing to refund and no penalty to cap to 3 months' fees. (2) The missing right is structural, not a negotiated concession. Our party is a bankruptcy-remote SPE whose servicing rights are pledged to the Indenture Trustee for the Noteholders; vesting removal in the Trustee/Controlling Class is standard ABS architecture and rating-agency criteria. An Issuer 30-day convenience right would also be exercised through the Administrator, which is Cellco itself (see p0351, p0358, where even the optional exits require Administrator consent and sit with the Class A Certificateholder, defined at p0668 as the Originators or their designee), so the right would be illusory while cutting against our own Noteholders. Inserting it is disproportionate under the "existing bargain" carve-out.

Recommendation: confirm a playbook carve-out for securitization transfer-and-servicing agreements, or, if the deal team wants a lever, pursue it as an Indenture/Controlling-Class direction right rather than an Issuer convenience termination. Flagged as needs_review rather than compliant because the clause does not literally meet the fallback, and rather than deviation because the model redline would not benefit our party.
